metadata.notes: A real, physically DIFFERENT process from BOIL/SIMMER, not the same result reached differently — the target never touches the liquid at all, cooked by water-vapor contact only (requiredTools: ['steamer_basket'], keeping the food elevated above requiredToolCapabilities' own isDeepVessel pot of water). Deliberately its OWN 'steamed' transformedState rather than reusing BOIL's shared 'boiled' the way SIMMER correctly does (see simmer.json's own sharedTransformedStateNote for why that was the right call there) — for potato specifically this is backed by a real, MEASURED compositional difference, not just gentler process framing: see potato.json's own steamNote for the cited vitamin-retention figures. For egg, the eaten result is closer to boiled egg's own (see egg.json's own steamNote for the real, different reason STEAM is still worth having there) — kept as the same fixed state name anyway, both because ActionOutputsSchema only supports one fixed transformedState per action (not a per-target override) and because 'this egg was steamed, not boiled' is still a real, distinct fact about HOW it was cooked even when the eaten result converges.
metadata.citationNote: durationSeconds' 600-2400s (10-40 minutes) range reflects a real, cited piece-size dependency (checked via multiple convergent consumer recipe sources this session), not a single point figure: small cubed/baby potatoes ~10-15 minutes, whole potatoes ~30-40 minutes; egg.json's own steamNote has the separate, more precise 12-minute figure for a whole steamed hard-cooked egg. See REFERENCES.md for the full citation list.
metadata.toolNote: requiredTools: ['steamer_basket'] + requiredToolCapabilities: ['isDeepVessel'] together — real steaming needs BOTH a vessel to hold a shallow layer of boiling water AND a basket/insert to keep the food out of that water, not one tool doing both jobs the way BOIL's single isDeepVessel requirement does. See steamer_basket.json's own notes for why this couldn't just reuse an existing tool/capability.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true (data-level, no duplication) — re-steaming an already-finished result risks overcooking, the same caveat every cooking action in this vocabulary already carries.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): same reasoning as boil.json/simmer.json — a real, elapsed-time thermal process. Not wired to place.ts/HEAT_PLACE (that machinery models a vessel's own contents temperature — water directly touching what's being heated — a steamer basket's contents are a materially different physical situation place.ts doesn't currently model at all, named as a real, separate gap rather than force-fit) — applyAction executes it atomically today.
metadata.requiresActiveAttentionNote: Added 2026-08-17 (DAG-execution ticket, action.ts's own requiresActiveAttention doc comment) — classified PASSIVE. A steamer basket over held-boiling water — hands-off once set up, the same profile as BOIL/BAKE.

verification.description: A fork/skewer meets little resistance when inserted — the same visual/tactile check simmer.json/par-fry.json/alkaline_parboil.json use for an identically-shaped continuous, elapsed-time process

hazards.note: Rising steam and the boiling water beneath the basket — a real, distinct scald risk (steam burns can be worse than liquid-water burns at the same temperature due to latent heat release on contact with skin), same severity tier as BOIL/SIMMER's own hot_liquid hazard
